title: Prioritizing Risk Factors in Helicopter Ditching Using Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process
content:
A Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (FAHP) identified system failure and human factors as the most critical helicopter ditching risks, providing an evidence-based framework for improving operational risk assessment, emergency preparedness, and aviation safety.


ABSTRACT

Helicopter operations in a maritime environment pose significant risks of hazardous situations and high-risk incidents, often forcing helicopters to ditch in an emergency. To understand the underlying causes of these events, this study uses a core dataset of 236 helicopter ditching incidents extracted from the NTSB database (2005–2022) to extend the previously proposed helicopter-ditching risk taxonomy by prioritizing the identified risk categories using expert-based Fuzzy AHP (FAHP). Consequently, this study aims to prioritize helicopter ditching risk factors using the Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (FAHP) based on expert judgment. The methodology uses pairwise comparisons evaluated by six aviation experts with experience in maritime operations, Triangular Fuzzy Numbers (TFNs) to handle uncertainty, and a Consistency Ratio (CR) check, with only judgments below 0.1 included in the final weight calculations. The FAHP results indicate that System Failure is the highest-ranked main risk factor (weight 0.343), followed by Human Factor (0.275). Ultimately, these prioritized risk factors provide practical decision support for maritime flight operations by guiding targeted pilot training, improving predictive maintenance protocols, and enhancing operational risk assessments during emergency procedures, specifically benefiting active pilots and flight crews who routinely operate helicopters in maritime and open-sea environments.
